A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same simulator, BA-NODE predictor, and predictive-shielding benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on prediction accuracy, safety generalization, and shielding across diabetes settings and age groups, including additional results in Appendices F and G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds hidden-size sensitivity, runtime and trigger-rate measurements, and imperfect-compliance experiments.

M1.justification: The simulator, BA-NODE architecture and training objective, context-conditioned adaptation, and predictive-shielding procedure are retained. The new hidden-size and masking-penalty experiments evaluate configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds evaluation at 75% and 50% patient compliance; v1 evaluates perfect compliance despite describing an acceptance mechanism. The simulated patient populations, diabetes settings, and clinical control task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The eight RL algorithms, unshielded and rule-based comparisons, and ITransformer/NODE prediction baselines are retained. The new analyses reuse existing methods; OnCRPO is an existing designation for CRPO, not an added comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate hidden sizes 16, 32, 64, and 128 and measure runtime and intervention frequency. Appendix I selects masking penalties from {-1, -5, -10, -20} separately for each algorithm and compliance level using highest mean TIR. Existing main-experiment splits, training budgets, and clinical metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens supplementary analysis: Appendix F.4 tests sensitivity to latent hidden size, Appendix H examines computational overhead and intervention frequency, and Appendix I stress-tests imperfect adherence. These address additional robustness and deployment questions beyond the retained basis-count, horizon, and adaptation analyses.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three-seed evaluation and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Appendix I explicitly follows this practice. The additional result tables do not establish an increased run count or a new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, but substantial operational and compliance results are added. Table 18 reports CPO runtimes of 345.816 seconds with predictive shielding versus 10.618 unshielded; Table 21 reports 80.76% shielded TIR under separately tuned 50% compliance. Table 3 changes the exception attribution from RCPO to CUP/PCPO, although its wording still contradicts PCPO's +0.19 Risk Index change.

T1.justification: Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, its Appendix B proof and hyperglycemia extension, and the simulator and model derivations are unchanged. The added analyses introduce no new formal guarantees or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same simulator, safety-generalization-gap, and predictive-shielding contributions, including the 13–14% TIR-gain claim. The appendix additions provide further evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly discusses the predictive shield's computational cost, the cheaper rule-based alternative, and implications of five-minute control intervals. Appendices F.4 and I interpret limited hidden-size sensitivity and functionality under partial adherence. Existing simulation and forecast-reliability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies hidden size 128 for the main predictor and documents CPU-only, SLURM-based runtime evaluation without GPU acceleration or inference optimization. Appendix I provides its selection grid but omits selected penalties. The differently displayed code links point to the same repositories.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. The Ray et al. benchmark reference changes its bibliographic location to an OpenAI report, without adding a different work or revising the scientific relationship.

P1.justification: v2 adds the new appendix sections and acknowledgments, updates cross-references, renames the impact statement heading, and makes limited wording and publication-header edits. The existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7 and Tables 18–21, relocates retained material, and renumbers subsequent appendix tables. Existing figures remain unchanged. Local presentation issues include the separated Table 7 caption and the incomplete 'Shielded (%)' column heading in the compliance tables.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity, runtime, and adherence analyses address useful gaps in v1 and make deployment costs more transparent. Their benefit is limited by condition-specific best-TIR penalty selection, undisclosed selected penalties, and remaining table-label and caption errors. The core method, theory, and original results remain intact, yielding a limited overall strengthening.
